plan.curriculum: Mathematics 2.0, Measurement, Year 5 (VC2M5M04): estimate and construct angles in degrees with a protractor, including reflex angles
plan.shape: short cycles: estimate, then construct, then reflex, each modelled and tried straight away, because the three moves build on each other
plan.criticalFeature: estimate first against 90° and 180°, then measure; a reflex angle is 360° minus the inside angle
decisionPoints: the choice check on reflex angles
the hinge: find the reflex angle
plan.anchor: quarter turn 90°, half turn 180°, full turn 360°
plan.catchUp: Missed Session 1? Show the angle-names chart and model one measurement on the inner scale before the practice round.

manipulatives: A protractor and a ruler for every student
A large demonstration protractor, or the on-screen protractor
studentTools: Printed Worksheet for every student; Extension and Supported Worksheet as needed
routineIcons: Write it, chin it, show me
boardSetup: The anchor on the board: quarter turn 90°, half turn 180°, full turn 360°

resources.subtitle: You need a protractor, a ruler and a sharp pencil.

items.prompt: Estimate, then measure.
Estimate, then measure.

example.prompt: Draw an angle of 50° on this arm.
steps: Centre on the dot, 0 on the arm.
Rule from the corner through the dot.

items.prompt: Draw an angle of 40° on this arm. Then name it.
Draw an angle of 115° on this arm. Then name it.
Measure the inside angle. Then work out the reflex angle.
Fill the gaps. Some go backwards!

example.prompt: A skier turns a quarter turn, then another quarter turn. How far did she turn?

items.prompt: A snowboarder spins a full turn, then another quarter turn. How many degrees is that altogether?
Mia estimated the angle of a skater's arms, then measured it. Find her mistake and fix it.
work: My protractor says 150°, so the protractor must be wrong.
items.answer: The estimate was wrong, not the protractor. 150° is obtuse, so compare with 90° first: it is well over 90°.

sections.title: Build a triangle
sections.intro: You can build a triangle from a base and two angles. Draw the base, draw an angle at each end, and where the arms cross is the third corner.

steps: Draw 50° at each end, facing in.
Where the arms cross is the top corner.

items.prompt: Build a triangle: base 7 cm, angles of 60° and 60°. Measure the third angle.
Build a triangle: base 6 cm, angles of 90° and 40°. Measure the third angle.
Add the three angles in each triangle. What do you notice? Do you think it is always true?
items.answer: Each set adds to 180°. It is always true for a triangle.

items.prompt: A triangle has angles of 90° and 50°. What is the third angle?

example.prompt: My inside angle is a quarter turn. What is my reflex angle?

items.prompt: My reflex angle is 3 times my inside angle. Together we make a full turn. What are we?
My reflex angle is 200°. What is my inside angle, and what is its name?

steps: Hold a book corner on it.
It is just smaller than the corner.

items.prompt: Estimate this angle.
items.hint: Half of a square corner is 45°.

items.prompt: Which is the best estimate?
items.hint: A square corner and half of one more.

items.prompt: Estimate this angle.
items.hint: Almost a straight line, and a straight line is 180°.

items.prompt: Which is the best estimate?
items.hint: Much smaller than a square corner.

steps: Dot at 60, then rule to the corner.

slides.notes: Session 2 of our angles week: today we estimate angles, draw them, and find the really big ones.
Before you start, put a protractor, a ruler and a sharp pencil on every desk. Print the Worksheet for everyone, and a few copies of the Extension and the Supported Worksheet.

slides.title: Decimal to fraction
prompts: Write 0.4 as a fraction in its simplest form.

beats: SAY: Let's warm up with fractions, decimals and percentages again.
ASK: How would you write 0.4 as a fraction in its simplest form?
20 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 2/5. ACCEPT: 4/10, then simplified
SCAN boards, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal and move on.
Less -> write 4/10, divide the top and bottom by 2 together, re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: Four tenths simplifies to two fifths.
Tick it or fix it.
trap: stopping at 4/10.
Fix: ask what divides both numbers, and they simplify it.
notes.prep: Daily Review from Term 3 Week 9. Keep the whole review under 6 minutes.

beats: ASK: What is 10 percent of 350?
15 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 35
SCAN boards.
80%+ -> reveal and move on.
Less -> 10% is one tenth, so share 350 into 10 equal parts. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: It's 35, because 10 percent is one tenth of 350.
Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing 3.5 or 350.
Fix: remind them 10% is one tenth, and they divide by 10.
notes.prep: Term 3 Week 9 retrieval: a percentage of an amount.

beats: ASK: What is one fifth plus three tenths?
30 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 5/10 or 1/2
SCAN boards for a common denominator.
80%+ -> reveal, then on to Fluency.
Less -> rename one fifth as two tenths on the strips, re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: One fifth is the same as two tenths, so we get five tenths,
which is one half. Tick it or fix it.
trap: adding across to get 4/15.
Fix: rename to tenths first, and they add again.
notes.prep: Spaced retrieval from Term 3 Week 8: adding related fractions.

slides.title: Add with the written method: 3 digits

beats: SAY: Now for some written addition.
Line up the places, and always start with the ones.
ASK: Use the written method to solve this one.
30 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 923
SCAN boards for the regrouped digits.
80%+ -> reveal, then the next one.
Less -> model the ones and the regroup together on the board, re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: The answer is 923.
Tick it or fix it, and check every regroup.
trap: forgetting to add a regrouped ten.
Fix: circle each carried digit, and they add that column again.
notes.prep: Addition fluency: 3 digits, then 4, then 5. Keep the whole block under 6 minutes.

slides.title: Add with the written method: 4 digits

beats: SAY: Now it's 4 digits.
It's the same method, just one more column.
ASK: Use the written method to solve this one.
45 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 8 043
SCAN boards for the regrouped digits.
80%+ -> reveal, then the next one.
Less -> model the ones and the regroup together on the board, re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: The answer is 8 043.
Tick it or fix it, and check every regroup.
trap: forgetting to add a regrouped ten.
Fix: circle each carried digit, and they add that column again.

slides.title: Add with the written method: 5 digits

beats: SAY: Now it's 5 digits.
It's the same method, just one more column.
ASK: Use the written method to solve this one.
60 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 84 403
SCAN boards for the regrouped digits.
80%+ -> reveal, then the learning intention.
Less -> model the ones and the regroup together on the board, re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: The answer is 84 403.
Tick it or fix it, and check every regroup.
trap: forgetting to add a regrouped ten.
Fix: circle each carried digit, and they add that column again.

slides.learningIntention: We are learning to estimate angles and draw them accurately with a protractor.
successCriteria: I can estimate an angle using 90° and 180° as guides.
I can draw an angle of a given size with a ruler and protractor.
I can find a reflex angle by measuring the inside angle and subtracting from 360°.

beats: POINT to the learning intention.
SAY: Yesterday we measured angles.
Today we're estimating them, drawing them, and finding the really big ones.
SAY: Let's read our I can statements together.
Cue: Everyone, together, on three.
SAY: We'll estimate first, because it helps us check our measuring.
Drawing an angle is our big goal today.
notes.prep: SC1 estimating is reachable for all; SC2 drawing an angle is the core; SC3 reflex angles is the exit evidence and the stretch.

slides.title: Name it, then estimate it
slides.prompt: Is it closer to 90° or to 180°?

beats: POINT to the angle.
SAY: Here's an angle. Let's name it first, then have a go at its size.
ASK: What do we call this kind of angle?
10 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: obtuse
ASK: Is it closer to 90 degrees or to 180 degrees? Write your estimate.
15 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: closer to 180, about 140
SCAN boards for estimates between 120 and 160.
80%+ -> name the reasoning you saw, then move on.
Less -> hold up a book corner and a ruler edge, compare, re-ask.
trap: estimating under 90 for an obtuse angle.
Fix: name it first, and they estimate again above 90.
notes.prep: Launch after the LI retrieves Session 1 names and starts benchmark estimating. Under 4 minutes.

slides.meaning: A careful guess using what you know.
slides.example: It is a bit more than a right angle, so about 100°.

notes.answer: a careful guess using what you know
beats: POINT to the word.
SAY: This word is estimate. Say it with me: estimate.
SAY: An estimate is a careful guess, not a wild one.
For angles, we compare with a quarter turn and a half turn.
ASK: Would 100 degrees be a good estimate for a right angle?
10 sec. Cue: Thumbs only, voices off. Show me... now.
EXPECT: thumbs sideways: close, but a right angle is exactly 90
trap: treating an estimate as a wild guess.
Fix: ask which turn it's close to, and they estimate again.
notes.prep: Estimating keeps measurements honest: a reading that is far from the estimate means the wrong scale.

slides.title: Estimate, then measure
steps: It is more than 90° and less than 180°.
About a third of the way from 90° to 180°: about 120°.

beats: MODEL comparing with a square corner.
SAY: Watch how I estimate this one.
It's more than a quarter turn, but well short of a half turn.
POINT between 90 and 180.
SAY: It's about a third of the way from 90 to 180,
so my estimate is about 120 degrees.
ASK: Now read the protractor. How close was my estimate?
15 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 118
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: It's 118 degrees, so my estimate of 120 was close.
That tells me I read the right scale.
trap: reading 62 on the other row.
Fix: compare with the estimate, and they read it again.
notes.stretch: Estimate three angles around the room, then measure them.
notes.help: Say quarter turn or half turn first, then estimate.
notes.prep: Estimating is a check on measuring: an answer far from the estimate means the wrong scale. SC1.

slides.title: Draw an angle of 70°
steps: Rule an arm and mark the vertex.
Centre on the vertex, 0 on the arm.
Count up from that 0 and dot at 70.
Rule from the vertex through the dot.

beats: MODEL the arm and the vertex dot.
SAY: To draw an angle, I start with one straight arm
and a dot for the corner.
MODEL the centre and the 0.
SAY: Now the centre goes on the dot, and the 0 sits on my arm.
ASK: Which row of numbers do I count along to reach 70?
10 sec. Cue: Voices off. Point... now. Hold your point.
EXPECT: pointing to the inside row
REVEAL after pointing is scanned.
SAY: It's the row that starts at 0 on my arm.
I put a dot at 70, then rule a line through it.
trap: dotting at 110 on the other row.
Fix: check it looks acute, and they draw it again.
notes.stretch: Draw a 70 degree angle on an arm pointing left.
notes.help: Use the Supported Worksheet, where the protractor is printed on.
notes.prep: Drawing is measuring in reverse: the same centre, the same 0. SC2.

beats: POINT to the big arc.
SAY: This angle goes the long way round.
My protractor only goes to 180, so I can't measure it directly.
MODEL measuring the inside angle.
SAY: So instead, I measure the small angle inside. It's 60 degrees.
ASK: A full turn is 360 degrees. So what's the reflex angle?
15 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 300
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: 360 take away 60 is 300,
so the reflex angle is 300 degrees.
trap: subtracting from 180 to get 120.
Fix: point to the full turn on the anchor, and they redo it.
notes.stretch: Why do the inside angle and the reflex angle always make 360?
notes.help: Write 360 - ___ = ___ and fill in the inside angle.
notes.prep: The anchor does the work: a full turn is 360 degrees. SC3.

slides.title: Find the reflex angle
slides.prompt: The inside angle is 50°. What is the reflex angle?

options.misconception: gives the inside angle, not the reflex angle

beats: SAY: Here are three answers,
and only one of them uses a full turn.
ASK: The inside angle is 50 degrees. What's the reflex angle?
15 sec. Cue: Voices off. Point... now. Hold your point.
EXPECT: pointing to B
SCAN the room, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal, then cold call one student: Why isn't it A?
Less -> draw it: shade the small angle, trace the long way round. Re-ask.
REVEAL after pointing is scanned.
SAY: It's B. 360 take away 50 is 310.
trap: pointing to A.
Fix: ask how far a full turn goes, and they redo 360 - 50.
notes.prep: First decision point, on the step most students skip. Under 80% means rebuild with the demonstration protractor.

slides.title: Estimate first
slides.ask: Estimate this angle. Write your estimate.
slides.pivot: compare with a book corner and a ruler edge together
slides.followUp: cold call one board: Which turn did you compare it with?

items.say: It's 82 degrees, so an estimate close to 80 is spot on.
It's 155 degrees. Anything around 150 is a great estimate.
It's 30 degrees, about a third of a right angle.
It's 240 degrees. It's reflex, because it's past a half turn.
It's 100 degrees, just a little more than a right angle.

say: Write your best estimate on your board.
trap: estimates on the wrong side of 90.
Fix: name the angle first, then estimate.
notes.help: Say smaller than, about, or bigger than a quarter turn first.
notes.prep: Guided estimating: accept within about 10°. Reflex item tests the half-turn benchmark. SC1.

beats: SAY: This one is just for you. The inside angle is marked for you.
ASK: What's the reflex angle marked with the question mark?
20 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 320
SCAN every board, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal, then Your turn.
Less -> trace the full turn with a finger, 360 all the way round. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: It's 320 degrees, because 360 take away 40 is 320.
Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing 140.
Fix: ask what a full turn is, and they subtract from 360.
notes.prep: The hinge before independent work. Anyone who wrote 140 starts on the Supported Worksheet with the teacher.

slides.title: Your turn
slides.task: Estimate, draw and measure the angles on your worksheet.

beats: POINT to the steps.
SAY: Read each question carefully, solve it carefully, then check your answers.
SAY: If you finish, the Extension is your early finisher option.
Let's read the steps together. Cue: Everyone, together, on three.
CIRCULATE. Check drawn angles with your own protractor.
TIME: 20 minutes. Stop everyone once at 10 minutes to share a strategy.
trap: drawing from the wrong 0.
Fix: check against their estimate, and they draw it again.
notes.stretch: Extension: build triangles from angles, and reflex riddles.
notes.help: Supported Worksheet: protractors printed on, and a hint on every question.
notes.prep: Independent practice: estimate, draw, reflex angles and a sport problem with a mistake to fix. The sheet is evidence for SC1 to SC3.

slides.title: Show what you know
questions: Draw an angle of 125° on your board.

notes.answer: an obtuse angle of 125°. An acute angle means the wrong scale (55°)
beats: SAY: Here's the last one. Use your protractor to draw it on your board.
ASK: Can you draw an angle of 125 degrees?
60 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: an obtuse angle, about 125
RECORD who draws an acute angle, the wrong scale.
They start tomorrow's first check with the teacher.
trap: drawing 55 degrees.
Fix: none now. Record the name for tomorrow.
notes.prep: Exit evidence for SC2: an acute drawing shows the scale error at a glance. It drives tomorrow's grouping.

slides.reflectionPrompt: Tell your partner how estimating helps you measure.

notes.answer: open - listen for checking the reading against the estimate
beats: SAY: Let's read our I can statements together.
Cue: Everyone, together, on three.
ASK: How sure are you that you can draw an angle?
5 sec. Cue: Thumbs only, voices off. Show me... now.
EXPECT: thumbs up, sideways or down
RECORD each thumb down beside the exit board.
A thumb up with an acute drawing matters most.
ASK: Tell your partner how estimating helps you measure.
20 sec. Cue: Partner B first. You have 20 seconds. Go.
EXPECT: it shows me if I read the wrong scale
notes.prep: Read the self-assessment beside the exit evidence. SC2.
